entries.verdict: "I think these are the Swiss Army knife of headphones." He has owned his pair for 13 years. They block a lot of noise, are nearly indestructible and cost about $100, but he hates the coiled cable.

entries.verdict: "These are some of my favorite headphones that I own." They are cheap and dark-sounding with slow bass and poor imaging, but they beat laptop speakers and cheap buds: "Technically crap, but technically amazing."

entries.verdict: His regular open-back for work and editing. Durable, easy to drive and made in Austria. He says he would get these instead of spending thousands on fragile flagships.

entries.verdict: "These are excellent." These are MDR-7506 drivers inside industrial earmuffs. They block a huge amount of noise with no batteries, and he uses them all the time. He hates the coiled cable.

entries.verdict: "For most normal everyday people, I really would recommend these." They are grown-up, with Bose noise cancelling, but he wishes they sounded cleaner and hit harder.

entries.verdict: The original 'dirty buds' that cheap players copy. They are all mids with almost no sub-bass: "They're just heckin mid."

entries.verdict: "My favorite close back recommendation." They are comfortable, have deep flat bass and sound wide for a closed-back. He recommends the 80 ohm version.

entries.verdict: "For the spend these are flipping excellent." They feel cheap but are comfortable and fun, with a V-shaped sound. He suggests them for schools needing a room full of headphones.

entries.verdict: "A fun close back option and just really comfortable, built really nice." They have metal parts at under $50 and extra bass. He recommends them, especially on special.

entries.verdict: "I honestly recommend both of these" (alongside the KBEAR KS1). For about $20 you get extra bass with tasteful sparkle, a removable cable and a good mic. On sound he leans towards the KZ.

entries.verdict: He recommends them alongside the KZ ZSN Pro. The sound is great for about $20, they look nice in white, and he thinks the mic is slightly better than the KZ's.

entries.verdict: "Lots of people love them and I don't." They are fun but dark-sounding, and he finds the build fragile, the headband hair-pulling and the price too high for what they are.

entries.verdict: He calls them the Porta Pro's spiritual successor: "cheaper, better sounding, better built", and they come with a mic. The wires are very thin.

entries.verdict: "These sound like crap, they really do." He finds them muffled with no soundstage, and the cable is so noisy that he disqualified them.

entries.verdict: "I keep rating these because they keep being good." They fit well, have a quiet removable cable and tasteful extra bass and treble, and beat earbuds from much bigger brands.

entries.verdict: "Boy, Sennheiser's disqualified." He finds the sound just okay, the fit uncomfortable and the cable terribly noisy. The mic is good.

entries.verdict: "The FiiO FD5s, I really like these." They are a clear step up from the KZ, with smoother bass, a wider stage and a huge accessory kit. He found them fun for pop.

entries.verdict: "I hate how they sound." He says the top end is rubbish, they feel cheap, are uncomfortable and have an annoying cable, which makes the price worse.

entries.verdict: "The best sounding ones of the day." They are the most balanced and widest-sounding IEMs he tried, and beautifully built. He found himself using them the most.

entries.verdict: "My favorites are the Audeze LCD-2s." They are what he uses when he sits down to really listen, with fast planar bass and detail. They are heavy, squeeze his head and need lots of power.

entries.verdict: "They sound awesome, they are super comfortable." Even so, he quit them after two pairs: one was faulty, the hinge clicked, and the Bluetooth and software got in the way.

entries.verdict: He calls them great, with decent noise cancelling and good looks. He hates the intrusive modern-tech behaviour, the lights and the poor Bluetooth mic, and plans to go back to cables.

entries.verdict: "I come running back for the stems." They are the smallest, least intrusive buds, with the best controls and ambient mode, and the case is built like a tank.

entries.verdict: "If you get them, you're going to love them." Noise cancelling is better, but they clipped painfully at drum volumes. He says you pay for convenience, not sound.
entries.source: Auto-transcript of 'I got the new Apple AirPods Pros.'

entries.verdict: For convenience "the AirPods are really hard to beat". He likes the open, resting fit and the pocketable, solid case, but says sound-first listeners should buy cheap wired gear.
entries.source: Auto-transcript of 'I got the AirPod 3's.'

entries.verdict: "These sound fantastic, the bass is so lovely." He finds them huge, with a cheap-feeling case, and like all true-wireless buds he expects them to be thrown away within a few years.

entries.verdict: "Great sound, excellent little package", and a bit cheaper than AirPods Pro. He finds the mic poor and the touch controls annoying, and still prefers AirPods.
